evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Key terms (game, name, optional description) have a single clear interpretation in this context.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting via a URL is a clear mechanism with no materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: The action and input method are specific enough to avoid multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: ‘Items’ refers consistently to estimation items/stories in this backlog; no competing meaning is introduced.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item for (re-)estimation is clear and consistent with other stories.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to the estimation list is a single, clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: ‘Edit an item’ is clear in context (modify the text/description of the estimation item) without materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item from the list is a clear action with no alternative meanings.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: ‘Immediately’ is temporally vague and can be interpreted as (a) without waiting for all estimators, (b) instantly after moderator action, or (c) real-time as each estimate arrives—materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: ‘Average’ is ambiguous (mean vs median vs rounded mean; handling of non-numeric/special cards) leading to materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: ‘Show the same card’ is unclear about timing/conditions (e.g., after reveal vs during hidden phase; whether abstentions count), enabling different interpretations of when auto-fill triggers.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering a final estimate is clear; ‘agreed-upon’ indicates it is the team’s final value without implying a specific algorithm.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story within the same session is clear.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: ‘Spreadsheet’ and ‘import’ are underspecified (file type/format, required columns, mapping rules), allowing materially different interpretations of the required behavior.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste mechanism and expected input format are unclear (what is pasted, delimiters, multi-line handling), enabling different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: ‘Browse through’ is vague (list view, search, filters, pagination, ordering), leading to materially different requirements interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: ‘Transcript’ is not defined (what events/fields are included, ordering, whether chat/timestamps are included), allowing multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Depends on the ambiguous notion of ‘transcript’ (content/structure), so the export output is also ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV structure depends on what ‘transcript’ contains and how it is represented (rows/columns), which is not specified.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: ‘Delete’ can mean soft-delete vs hard-delete; ‘no longer stored’ could mean removed from UI vs physically erased—materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Required fields are explicitly listed; action is clear.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: ‘Account name’ is ambiguous given PP-021 distinguishes email address and username; it could refer to either.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: ‘Account details’ is underspecified (which fields can be changed: name, email, username, password, etc.), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: As with game deletion, ‘delete’/‘no longer stored’ can mean soft vs hard deletion and scope of data removal, leading to materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying dates/times in the user’s local timezone is a clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: ‘Password reminder’ is ambiguous (send existing password vs reset link vs temporary password), which are materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Two concrete card sets are explicitly enumerated, making the choice clear.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A numeric limit is explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via the provided URL and entering a name is clear.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: ‘Item’ consistently refers to the estimation item/story; no alternative meaning is suggested.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope (‘this session’) and object (‘items to estimate’) are clear in context.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given
evaluations.rationale: ‘Immediately’ is vague (real-time push vs periodic refresh vs after some action), leading to different functional expectations.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reveal condition (after all have estimated) and simultaneity are explicitly stated.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: The cutoff moment is unclear (is it when the last person selects, when reveal occurs, or both), and ‘all are shown’ depends on reveal mechanics—allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: ‘Prior estimates’ is ambiguous (earlier rounds in same game, earlier sessions/games, or historical across all time), leading to different data scope requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Scope (‘current round’) and information (mapping estimator to estimate) are clear.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Starting is clear, but key behavior is underspecified (who can start, whether multiple timers exist, visibility location), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: ‘As soon as we all play an estimate’ is ambiguous (when last person selects vs when estimates are revealed/locked), leading to different reset triggers.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: ‘Prior rounds’ could mean earlier in the same game/session only or include previous games; scope ambiguity affects data retrieval and UI.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Consistent ordering across draws is a clear requirement (even if the specific order is not specified, the constraint is unambiguous).

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: ‘Draw has not been completed’ is not defined (completed at last selection, at reveal, at moderator action), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: ‘Near where my cards are played’ is spatially vague (exact placement/association), leading to different UI requirements.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: ‘Compliant’ and ‘standards’ are ambiguous without specifying versions/levels and what constitutes compliance, enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: ‘Commonly used terms’ is vague (which terms, where sourced, completeness), allowing materially different scopes for the glossary.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: ‘As fast as possible’ is ambiguous and unbounded; also ‘the queries’ is unclear in scope (which queries), leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Target browsers/versions are explicitly listed; requirement intent is clear.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: ‘Where possible’ is subjective and allows materially different interpretations of required compliance level and exceptions.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: ‘Quickly’ is vague without thresholds and can be interpreted in materially different performance targets.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: ‘Use Unicode’ is underspecified (input only vs storage vs display; which components), allowing different interpretations of scope.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: ‘Sensible’ and ‘predictable’ are subjective and can lead to different URL design requirements.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: ‘Nice’ and ‘something goes wrong’ are vague (which errors, what content/design), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: ‘Non-identifiable’ is ambiguous without specifying anonymization/pseudonymization requirements and threat model; multiple materially different implementations are possible.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: ‘Some metrics’ is vague (which metrics, time range, granularity), allowing materially different interpretations of what must be provided.
